title: New Mexico sues Epstein attorney and accountant, accuses them of hiding sex trafficking operation
text:
New Mexico sues Epstein attorney and accountant, accuses them of hiding sex trafficking operation
New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez sued Jeffrey Epstein’s attorney and accountant on Wednesday, accusing them of concealing his sex trafficking operation at a Santa Fe-area ranch where the disgraced financier once entertained guests.
The lawsuit filed in federal court names Epstein's personal attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn as the two people the attorney general is seeking enforcement action against. The lawsuit also names the estate of Jeffrey Epstein and the 1953 Trust, which holds the assets for the estate.
The New Mexico Department of Justice alleges in the federal court complaint that Epstein ran a sex trafficking operation. The office also alleges Indyke and Kahn knowingly participated in the operation by using their positions and Epstein's accounts to finance and conceal alleged abuse.
The department claims Indyke and Kahn held leadership roles that managed financial accounts and authorized transactions that are connected to the trafficking operation. Torrez alleges that Indyke handled the 2011 transfer of the title for Zorro Ranch to an Epstein-controlled company.
The department alleged that both Indyke and Kahn benefited financially from the relationships with Epstein. It said Indyke received $16 million from Epstein, while Kahn received more than $10 million in a time period from 2011 through 2019. The lawsuit also said both are beneficiaries of the 1953 Trust and are co-executors of the Epstein estate who are involved in managing and distributing assets.
The lawsuit seeks to stop Indyke and Kahn from accepting any payments from Epstein's estate.
Torrez said Epstein’s estate holds more than $100 million, and that Indyke and Kahn “stand to benefit substantially” unless a court intervenes.
“Those resources rightfully belong in the hands of survivors,” the attorney general said, referring to victims of Epstein’s abuse.
Indyke worked as Epstein’s attorney for roughly two decades. Both he and Kahn have testified in a congressional committee that they did not know about Epstein’s abuse.
The announcement comes after agents with the attorney general's office searched Epstein's Zorro Ranch as part of a state investigation.   
The New Mexico Department of Justice is asking the court for the following:
- Prevent payments from Epstein's Estate to Indyke and Kahn during the period of litigation.
- Restrict the ability to authorize and receive estate payments
- Declare that the two engaged in racketeering and trafficking activity in violation of state and federal law
- Require the two to divest Epstein-related interests and restrict certain future investment activity
- Award compensatory and punitive damages, restitution and disgorgement of benefits to survivors
Epstein took his own life in August 2019 in a federal jail in New York City, where he was awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.
Epstein’s former girlfriend and close associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, is serving a 20-year prison sentence after her 2021 conviction on sex trafficking charges in New York. Witness testimony at Maxwell’s trial alleged she and Epstein had sexually abused women at the New Mexico ranch.
Epstein purchased the ranch in Stanley, New Mexico, a sparsely populated ranching community about 30 miles south of Santa Fe, in 1993. He built a 26,700-square-foot mansion with a sprawling courtyard, a living room roughly the size of the average American home, and a private airstrip and helipad.
Epstein never faced charges in New Mexico, though the state attorney general's office in 2019 confirmed that it was investigating and planned to forward its findings to federal authorities in New York. Hector Balderas, who was attorney general at the time, said the state’s outdated laws failed to protect children from abuse.
The property was sold by Epstein’s estate in 2023 — with proceeds going toward creditors — to the family of Don Huffines, a Republican recently appointed Texas’ state comptroller. Huffines said in a social media post the property has been renamed San Rafael Ranch and that his family plans to operate a Christian retreat there.
This story includes discussion of suicide. If you or someone you know needs help, the national suicide and crisis lifeline in the U.S. is available by calling or texting 988. There is also an online chat at 988lifeline.org.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Letter: Republicans are Trump enablers
text:
Letters submitted by BDN readers are verified by BDN Opinion Page staff. Send your letters to letters@bangordailynews.com
First a story about my father, born in 1926. This is relevant as it is about party politics. World War II was starting to wind down after he reached 17, and being worried about missing out, he was able to lie about his age and get in the Army at the tail end. A bit of shooting from foxholes he said, but mostly he was assigned to guard duty over POWs only a few years younger than him, conscripted Hitler Youth, they were 13, 14, 15, he said.
He also told us about the occupation once the war in Europe ended. The little German he first learned was for his work: “Halten,” or “Schnell” — “Stop!” or “Hurry up!” The first full sentence he learned was “Ich war kein Nazi!!” I was not a Nazi!
He heard that everywhere: POWs, mothers, bakers, tram conductors. Everyone was very eager to tell young Americans in uniform that: “Ich war kein Nazi!!” My father wondered, a whole big country of Germans and no one was a Nazi, then who the heck were we fighting? (Thanks Dad, one of the original “anti-fa!”)
Why am I voting Democrat? Not because I am a Democrat. Not because I am a liberal. But because I believe every Republican on my ballot, and on your ballot, is a Trump enabler. President Donald Trump can’t exist without these folks. They make Trump who he is.
I believe they have to go. All of them. Clean sweep. Vote them all out.
Paul Sheridan
Northport

title: Former NFL defensive end Allen Bailey dies at 37
text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV/Gray News) - Former NFL defensive end Allen Bailey has died at the age of 37.
Bailey, 37, played 10 seasons in the league and spent eight of them with the Kansas City Chiefs after being drafted by the team in the 2011 NFL Draft.
Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, who coached Bailey for six of his eight seasons in Kansas City, called Bailey “one of my favorite players” on Wednesday, acknowledging Bailey’s death during his weekly press conference.
“It’s terrible,” Reid said of any time a former player of his passes at a young age. “[Bailey] had a father who passed away young, too. It’s life, but it makes you sick.”
The Chiefs also issued a statement as an organization on Wednesday:
“Allen Bailey was an excellent teammate, generous man, and kind soul. We’re deeply saddened to hear of his passing, and our thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends.”
Patrick Mahomes, who was a teammate of Bailey for two seasons, shared a story Wednesday of the first time he walked into the locker room and saw Bailey.
“I step in the locker room and see Allen Bailey, and I’m like, ‘This isn’t the Big 12 anymore,’” Mahomes recalled of Bailey’s imposing figure. “It was surreal to see him, and I tell that story every single year. Obviously, it’s terrible to hear the news that we heard.
Mahomes added, “A great teammate. He was one of those glue guys on the team. He made plays and was the guy who made everything go. Terrible to hear that news. We’re praying for him and his family.”
In eight seasons with the Chiefs, Bailey started 61 of the 102 games he played in and tallied 207 tackles and 19.5 sacks. Bailey’s best statistical seasons came in 2014 and 2018, with a career-high six 6 sacks coming in his final season with the Chiefs and his lone touchdown, a fumble recovery scoop-and-score in Kansas City’s 54-51 shootout loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Nov. 19, 2018.
Following the 2018 campaign, Bailey signed a two-year contract with the Falcons in free agency. He appeared in 31 games with Atlanta before being released in February 2021.
Bailey was from the small town of Sapelo Island, Georgia, and made his way to the University of Miami, where he starred for the Hurricanes in college.
Bailey’s brother, Alford Bailey Jr., told TMZ that his body was discovered in his Florida home on Tuesday. No immediate cause of death was released.

title: Runner attempts world record with 50 marathons in 50 states
text:
Runner attempts world record with 50 marathons in 50 states
William Goodge, an ultramarathoner from London, England, is attempting to run 50 marathons in 24 days across all 50 U.S. states.
He's raising funds for cancer research and attempting a new world record.
"I am running a marathon distance in all 50 U.S. states," Goodge told sister station KMBC in Kansas City. "And I'm doing it in 24 days."
Goodge began running after his mother died from cancer a few years ago, making it his mission to support cancer research in her name.
"I was like, well, I can (be) numb, or I can turn this emotional pain I've got into something positive," Goodge said.
He discovered his talent for running nearly 10 years ago.
"I'm not bad at this sport," he said.
Over the past eight years, Goodge has run thousands of miles, including across the U.S., Australia, and the length of the U.K.
"I've run thousands of miles over the past eight years, running across the U.S., running across Australia, and the length of the U.K.," Goodge said.
His Kansas City runs marked days nine and 10 of his 24-day journey, including participation in the Garmin Marathon race on Saturday.
"I need to do all the marathons in five hours or less to stay on time, so it's high-pressure, and a five-hour marathon isn't that fast, but doing 50 back-to-back, it's insane," Goodge said.
Despite the physical and mental challenges, Goodge hopes his efforts inspire others.
"Emotional pain can be pushed toward something positive," he said.

title: Rapper convicted of murdering woman, unborn child writes letter to judge asking for death penalty
text:
(Gray News) – A rapper from Tampa sent a letter to the judge presiding over his case asking for the death penalty.
Billy Adams, known as “Ace NH,” was convicted in September of the murder of 22-year-old Alana Sims and her unborn child, WTSP reported.
At the time, a jury recommended Adams be executed, but the official sentencing hearing is scheduled for Dec. 1.
Adams mailed a handwritten letter to Judge Mark Wolfe asking him to honor the jury’s decision.
“I want to waive mitigation at this hearing, and I want to be sentenced to what the jury voted to give me,” Adams wrote. “My lawyers explained mitigation to me and they explained the consequences of waiving mitigation.”
Adams went on to write that he understood what he was giving up and he doesn’t have an issue with the death penalty.
“I’m writing to put this on the record,” he said.
The letter concludes with Adams writing, “I have asked my lawyers to respect my wishes when we go to court.”
Just because Adams is requesting the death penalty doesn’t mean he will automatically be sentenced to death. A judge will decide that during the hearing in December.
Family members told WTSP Sims was five months pregnant when she was killed. She was found lying dead on the street in February 2023.
According to WTSP, the woman’s 1-year-old son was found unharmed, sleeping in an SUV next to her body.

title: Meta Q3 revenue tops estimates and Zuckerberg says Muse accounts have topped 10 million
text:
Meta Platforms said Wednesday that its third-quarter profit jumped more than threefold, as revenue climbed sharply.
The parent company of Facebook and Instagram reported net income of $9.86 billion, or $3.83 per share, for the July-September period. That’s up from a profit of $2.71 billion, or $1.05 per share, in the same period a year earlier.
Revenue grew 26% to $64.60 billion, up from $51.24 billion in the prior-year quarter and above the $63.34 billion expected by Wall Street analysts.
In August, Meta reached an $18 billion settlement with 48 U.S. states over the effects of social media on teen mental health. The company agreed to take steps to keep children under 13 off Instagram and Facebook and teens ages 14 and 18 in age-appropriate accounts.
Excluding the impact of a $9.89 billion charge related to this agreement, the company’s third-quarter earnings would have been $7.40 per share, Meta said. The-year ago quarter included a one-time tax charge of nearly $16 billion.
“We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone — including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model,” said CEO Mark Zuckerberg in a statement. “Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we’re seeing velocity across the board.”
During a call with analysts, Zuckerberg noted that more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up accounts for Muse, the personal artificial intelligence agent the company launched in August.
Meta said the number of daily active users on its “family of apps” — Facebook, Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp — grew 3% from a year earlier to an average of 3.64 billion.
The Menlo Park, California-based company had 66,775 employees as of Sept. 30, a decrease of 15% year-over-year.
For the current quarter, Meta is forecasting revenue in the range of $73 billion to $76 billion, the midpoint of which is higher than the $73.65 billion analysts are expecting.
Total expenses were $51.61 billion, an increase of 68% year-over-year. This includes the charge stemming from its multistate legal settlement.
Meta’s shares closed up 0.5% in regular trading Wednesday. The shares rose 2.9% in after-hours trading after the results were released. The stock is up 5.7% so far this year.

title: Macron calls claims by Trump and others blaming Muslim migrants for French riots ‘stupid’
text:
PARIS (AP) — French President Emmanuel Macron said Wednesday that foreign leaders — including those “on the other side of the Atlantic” — were seeking to exploit France’s tense social climate for political gain following a weekend of street violence and looting.
Protests over soaring living costs have led to widespread rioting and looting that have drawn worldwide attention and shocked many French citizens. U.S. President Donald Trump has used the violence to rally his political supporters, making unsubstantiated claims that Muslim migrants are responsible for the unrest, and urging Macron to “close your borders and take control before it is too late!”
Macron responded by saying there “has been foreign manipulation of information in the aftermath” of the looting in Paris and other French cities last weekend. “And that has led to comments that are as unacceptable as they are stupid, from many people, including foreign leaders,” he said.
Asked by a reporter if he was referring to Trump, Macron replied: “Among others.” He added that there have been “AI-generated images depicting scenes that never actually happened in France. We’ve had people claiming that we were invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is completely false.”
Macron did not specify which AI-generated images he was referring to, nor how he knew the content was false.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said his office can provide the countries concerned with the necessary clarification, “to help them avoid spreading or amplifying false information and making baseless claims on social media.”
Macron and Trump once enjoyed a good relationship but Trump regularly mocks the French president in his public speeches.
“The fact is, all the people who are speaking ill of our country right now are people who don’t love our country,” Macron said. “So those people really bother me.”
“When I see leaders who are in the middle of election campaigns, whether in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic — who sometimes naively repeat AI-generated content or spread narratives that certain circles are clearly trying to promote about what happened in France — they’re using our country for their own political campaigns,” said Macron. “And we don’t need that.”
Macron secures diesel supplies
Macron was speaking in Qatar at the end of a tour of key energy suppliers in Gulf Arab states, where he secured an additional 100,000 metric tons of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates, with a further 100,000 tons to be confirmed in Bahrain.
Macron’s office said he traveled to the Middle East to find solutions to the energy crisis and rising energy prices, and to secure supplies of oil, gas, diesel and jet fuel.
The Élysée said nearly 295,000 additional tons of diesel per month could be secured, including supplies from Saudi Arabia — equivalent to more than 10% of France’s monthly diesel consumption. Macron later traveled to Saudi Arabia to meet Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman “to continue efforts to secure and diversify oil and gas supplies,” according to his office.
Earlier this month, the Group of Seven wealthy democracies agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products, beginning with substantial quantities of diesel after the fuel’s price hit a record high in the United States.
“I would remind you that France initiated the G7 meeting that led to the release of strategic reserves, which, through implementation at the national level, will help bring down prices starting in early November,” Macron said.
New protests planned in France on Thursday and Saturday
Petrol, energy and food prices have surged in recent months, and it remains to be seen whether Macron’s announcement will ease protesters’ anger. He said the additional diesel supplies addressed “some of the anxieties.”
“I also hear the concerns of our high school and university students. Those concerns stem from other factors, but in any case, I think things are moving in the right direction,” he added.
High school students have raised concerns about underfunded schools, dilapidated facilities and staff shortages, particularly in lower-income neighborhoods. Some also say school days, which often run from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., are exhausting and the university admissions system is complex and unfair.
France has had two consecutive quiet nights since the weekend’s unrest. Curfews have been imposed in parts of several major cities, including small areas of Paris.
Further protests are planned for Thursday and Saturday following calls from student unions and groups within the “yellow vest” movement, whose demonstrations over fuel prices shook France in 2018 and 2019.
Paris police said Wednesday they would ban Thursday’s planned protest in the French capital, citing concerns for public safety and the protection of property.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who met union representatives on Wednesday, said a “massive” security operation was planned for Saturday to prevent a repeat of the violence by small groups of rioters that had exposed shortcomings in security measures.
“We are using the legal means at our disposal to prevent further incidents of this kind,” Macron said. “Those who intend to cause disturbances in city centers next Saturday will be prevented from doing so. Tomorrow, we will also have a very detailed update on the implementation of these measures, including anticipation, intelligence gathering and security, not just for Saturday, but also for the coming weeks.”

title: Light-colored Pickup Sought In I-95 Hit-and-run That Injured Maine DOT Worker
text:
Maine Police Release Truck Photo in Hit-and-Run Search
Maine State Police released a photo of a truck and trailer they believe were involved in an I-95 incident that sent a Maine DOT worker to the hospital.
Maine State Police are Looking for the Driver in an I-95 Hit-and-Run Crash
Witnesses told police the vehicle involved in the crash was a light-colored pickup truck, towing a black dump trailer.
State Police say they believe the photo released this week is the vehicle that caused the crash and then drove away without stopping.
READ MORE: Maine Fire Marshal Has Safety Tips for Anyone with a Woodstove
The incident happened on I-95 in Pittsfield on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:17 am.
Maine DOT Worker Was Seriously Injured When Hit By a Construction Barrel
Maine Department of Transportation workers were unloading construction barrels from a truck as traffic passed by, on the other side of a row of concrete Jersey barriers.
A vehicle, believed to be the one in the photo released by the police, struck a Jersey barrier on the right, causing a construction barrel to strike a worker in the construction zone.
The pickup truck continued northbound without stopping.
Witnesses say the driver allegedly turned around as the crash happened and then drove away.
The injured worker, 56-year-old Richard Smart of Westfield, was transported to Northern Light Sebasticook Valley Hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries.
He has since been released from the hospital.

Anyone who recognizes the vehicle in the photo or has information about the driver is asked to contact the Bangor Regional Communications Center at 207-973-3700, extension 9, and ask to speak with Trooper Klayton Peckham.
Maine State Police remind drivers to slow down, remain alert, and use extra caution when traveling through construction zones.
Roadside workers are often just a few feet away from moving traffic, and a moment of inattention can have devastating consequences.

title: California state workers begin 1-day strike over return-to-office mandate, pay and healthcare
text:
SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — California state workers began a one-day strike Wednesday, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom’s administration to agree to a new contract that increases workers’ pay, ensures affordable healthcare access and allows more flexibility for remote work.
SEIU Local 1000, the largest union for California government workers which represents more than 100,000 employees, including auditors, nurses and counselors, will picket in cities across the state for the first time since the union’s founding in 2004. Members overwhelmingly voted to authorize the strike earlier this month, accusing the state of failing to bargain in good faith after their contract expired in June.
“We are going on strike because we know the Newsom administration can and must do better,” Anica Walls, the union’s president, said in a statement. “They must return to the table and bargain in good faith toward a contract that allows state workers to afford groceries, childcare, rent and other necessities.”
The strike follows an order by Newsom requiring state workers to return to the office four days a week by July 1. Newsom, who’s preparing to leave office in January and eyeing a 2028 presidential run, argued that the mandate would improve workplace collaboration and innovation, which will help government better serve the public. He vetoed a bill backed by the union last month that would have required state agencies to provide a written justification for requiring workers to report to the office.
The California Department of Human Resources said it was coordinating with the union and with state departments, which have contingency plans in case government operations are disrupted by the strike.
“The department remains focused on achieving a fair and responsible agreement and continues to be available at the bargaining table,” it said in a statement.
The union argues that remote work saves the state money it would otherwise spend on office space and improves people’s work-life balance.
The union is also pushing for the state to raise workers’ salaries by 20% over the next three years and increase the state contribution toward employees’ healthcare costs.

title: Susan Collins’ biggest backer airs a country-song attack on Troy Jackson’s family
text:
Politics
Our political journalists are based in the Maine State House and have deep source networks across the partisan spectrum in communities all over the state. Their coverage aims to cut through major debates and probe how officials make decisions. Read more Politics coverage here.
The Republican super PAC that has spent heavily to reelect U.S. Sen. Susan Collins is running a country song on Maine radio that mocks her Democratic opponent, Troy Jackson, for having children with his second cousin.
The ad from the Senate Leadership Fund, which surfaced Tuesday, calls Jackson “weird,” a “freak” and a “creep” because “he has two kids with his cousin.”
“If he’ll screw his own family, he’ll screw yours too,” the chorus goes.
It’s one of a series of scorched-earth ads the group, which is tied to Senate Republican leaders and is the biggest spender in the Maine race, launched against Jackson over the weekend. Another calls the former Maine Senate president “a crook and a creep.”
Collins told reporters in Lewiston on Wednesday that the ad should come down. The attacks came two weeks before Election Day in a toss-up election that could decide control of the U.S. Senate.
Jackson and Lana Pelletier, a social worker from Allagash, have been together for nearly 40 years and have two adult sons. The Maine Wire reported this summer that they are second cousins, and Collins raised it herself in a September interview with Politico.
Pelletier pushed back in a Bangor Daily News opinion piece published Wednesday, saying Collins and her allies have mocked her family and children.
“I never imagined [Collins] and her allies would stoop this low,” she wrote.
She also disputed again a 1988 police report, exclusively reported by the BDN in August, which says Jackson punched a man at a Fort Kent home when he was 19. Jackson paid a fine. Pelletier told an officer that night that Jackson “pushed her around,” according to the report, but she has said she doesn’t remember saying it and that the statement isn’t accurate.
The Senate Leadership Fund and an offshoot are the biggest outside spenders in the race. They have booked nearly $50 million in Maine ads, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. They anchor a Republican network of super PACs and nonprofits that has booked about $126 million in ads to reelect Collins.
Democrats have also gone negative. WinSenate, a super PAC aligned with the party’s Senate campaign arm, has booked $38.6 million in Maine. One of its ads late last month misleadingly tied Collins to Jeffrey Epstein. Collins bemoaned those ads in Farmington on Tuesday.
“I have had tough races, always, always, but this is the first time where there have been nonstop lies about me and my record, character assassination,” she said. “I think it’s very disappointing that Chuck Schumer, Troy Jackson and their allies have sunk to this level.”

title: 9-year-old boy attacked by stranger while waiting for school bus, police say
text:
HENRICO, Va. (WWBT/Gray News) - A Virginia woman is facing charges after she allegedly punched a 9-year-old boy in the face at his school bus stop.
Henrico Police say 47-year-old Marie Tulette Marsh approached Ratcliffe Elementary School students waiting at their bus stop around 7:30 a.m. Friday. She then allegedly attacked a 9-year-old boy she didn’t know as the bus was pulling up.
A nearby resident, who didn’t want to go on camera, said he ran outside after he heard the victim scream for help. He said he saw a woman punching the boy in the face. The man said he rescued the boy, brought him to his front porch and called 911.
Police arrested Marsh, who is now facing an assault and battery charge. Investigators say the victim suffered injuries to his face but is expected to recover.
Earl Thomas, who lives nearby, is still in shock to hear about what happened in his neighborhood.
“I was devastated,” he said. “My nieces and nephews grew up in this area, and they stayed at this bus stop. So, actually, it was devastating to know that anything like that would even happen in this area and at a bus stop.”
Ratcliffe Elementary Principal Joy Reed said this was an isolated incident. She said counselors are helping support the students who ride that bus, and she plans to visit the bus stop throughout the week to reassure students about their safety and monitor the situation.
For Thomas, the circumstances are making him more aware of his surroundings.
“I’m looking around more obvious to what’s going on at the bus stop,” he said. “It’s definitely bringing awareness. You can’t be too comfortable now.”
Online court records show Marsh is set to have a hearing on Dec. 14.

title: Airbnb announces new rules for hosts, limiting checkout chores for guests
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Airbnb to limit checkout chores hosts can ask guests to do, banning bed stripping and laundry requirements
Airbnb has unveiled new rules for hosts that will limit the kinds of chores hosts can ask guests to complete before they check out.
Related video above: Dream vacation or costly scam? How to tell the difference
The updated policy goes into effect next month and outlines what hosts can ask guests to do. It has established seven standardized house rules that guests can find more easily before booking.
Under the new policy, hosts cannot require guests to:
- Wash and put away dishes
- Strip beds
- Start a load of laundry
- Take garbage off-site
- Avoid using a listed amenity
"All house rules and requests must be disclosed in the designated section of the listing page at the time of booking, so that guests can evaluate whether the home is a good fit before they book," Airbnb wrote in its policy.
However, hosts can still ask guests to place used dishes in the sink, gather used towels, and sort trash and recycling into designated indoor bins.
Airbnb is also standardizing house rules covering:
- Pets
- Smoking
- Quiet hours
- Events
- Commercial photography
- Maximum overnight guests
- Locking up at checkout
These new rules will take effect on Nov. 20.
"If a violation persists, it may result in a notice on the listing page flagging the issue to guests, reduced listing visibility in search, or other action under our Terms of Service," Airbnb said.

title: Here are 3 Maine high school football games to watch in Week 8
text:
This season, Varsity Maine reporters will offer up suggestions each week for three games that are worth a drive to watch in person, with a brief explanation of why we think these games are worth a fan’s time.
It’s Week 8 of the Maine high school football season — the final week for most of the state, but the penultimate week for Class A and C teams.
Some teams are still fighting for postseason spots, while others have clinched berths but are seeking a higher seed.
Here are three games to keep on your radar:
Kennebunk (6-1) at Marshwood (6-1), 6 p.m. Friday
Friday’s clash between the Rams and the Hawks could be a preview of the Class B South final. It no doubt will determine the top seed in the region.
After starting the season 1-1, Kennebunk has won five games in a row. The Rams are coming off a hard-fought 20-14 victory over Westbrook. Ethan White scored two touchdowns for Kennebunk, which has a deep group of running backs and a productive passing game led by Giovanni D’Elia.
Marshwood was undefeated until last weekend, when it lost to Biddeford, 37-14. The Hawks have shredded most of their opponents with a relentless rushing attack, but their top two running backs are questionable because of injuries.
Lisbon (5-2) at Freeport (5-2), 6 p.m. Friday
Despite these teams having the same record, Lisbon is currently fourth in the Class D South Crabtree standings, while Freeport is in first place.
The Greyhounds lost to second-place Winthrop/Monmouth/Hall-Dale 34-3 in the season opener but are 5-1 since then and bring a three-game winning streak to Freeport.
Freeport has two close losses, against Class D North leader Winslow (14-6) and Class C contender Wells (28-24). Even with starting quarterback Andrew Thomas injured, the Falcons defeated Morse and Dirigo the past two weeks, and they can clinch the No. 1 seed by defeating Lisbon.
Bonny Eagle (7-0) at Thornton Academy (7-0), 1 p.m. Saturday
Saturday’s matinee is not only a potential Class A South final preview, but also features the top-two teams in the Varsity Maine poll.
Thornton has the recent upper-hand. The Trojans were victorious in both of last season’s matchups — 42-21 in the regular season and 40-28 in the regional final.
Thornton’s multifaceted offense is tough to stop. Five players have rushed for 160 yards or more, led by Brennan Tabor with 634 yards. Noah Fullerton helms a prolific passing attack, completing 42 of 60 passes for 772 yards and 16 scores. His top targets are Logan LeBlanc (18 catches, 454 yards, nine TDs) and Logan O’Keefe (11 catches, 110 yards, four TDs), but eight players have caught passes. Tabor, also one of the state’s top defensive players, has scored a team-best 14 touchdowns.
Bonny Eagle quarterback Lucas Klehn is a touchdown machine and the player the Golden Trojans will have to watch for most. Klehn has contributed nine touchdowns in the Scots’ last two games — a passing touchdown and four rushing touchdowns against Oxford Hills on Oct. 9 and four rushing TDs against Exeter (New Hampshire) on Oct. 15. But Klehn isn’t the Scots’ only weapon. Drew Gervais, the state’s fastest sprinter, is the top receiving target, while Ben Noe and Ben Havu have both rushed for more than 300 yards.

title: Read the poem ‘Monument Square’ by Mark Evan Chimsky
text:
This week’s poem, by Mark Evan Chimsky, begins with a glimpsed moment between two men, and finds in it a glorious celebration of intimacy, potential and freedom. I love this poem’s careful and tender attention to each man’s posture, gaze and gesture, and its euphoria at their clear and open love.
Chimsky’s poems and essays have appeared in The Gay & Lesbian Review, The Muleskinner Journal, The Sunlight Press, and The Three Rivers Poetry Journal. Mark is a recipient of the Anna Davidson Rosenberg Award as New/Emerging Poet. In addition, Mark is an affiliated faculty member teaching at Emerson College in Boston, and a playwright, whose play “Meeting Fingerman” was winner of the Honegger Prize for Best Short Play 2024. His one-act “The Secret Muse” debuted at the Wisconsin Shakespeare Festival.
Poets, please note that submissions to Deep Water are open now and through the end of the year. Deep Water is especially eager to share poems by Black writers, writers of color, indigenous writers, LGBTQ+ writers, and other underrepresented voices. Find a link to submit credits at mainewriters.org/deep-water.
Monument Square
What does it mean, this one man tying 
another’s shoe? Both are in their twenties or so, lean 
in their short-sleeve shirts too dark 
for the sunlit day. Perhaps brothers, one doing 
what the other wishes he could do. 
But the tenderness in the way he knots 
the laces is more than brotherly 
and there’s boldness in his gaze 
as he keeps the other’s eyes in view. 
Though he’s the one who kneels 
his hand holds more than just the shoe. 
They both understand 
that power can shift with the imperceptible 
lift of a hand or foot. 
I have never seen such giving 
or such taking, 
where intimacy, like jazz, is a constant 
riff on possibility— 
one man ties the other’s shoe 
and then ravenously they kiss. 
– Mark Evan Chimsky
Megan Grumbling is a poet and writer who lives in Portland. Deep Water: Maine Poems is produced in collaboration with the Maine Writers & Publishers Alliance. “Monument Square,” ©2026 by Mark Evan Chimsky, appears by permission of the author. Submissions to Deep Water are open now and through the end of the year. For more information, go to mainewriters.org/deep-water.

title: Tom Cruise to receive life achievement award from the American Film Institute
text:
Tom Cruise to receive life achievement award from the American Film Institute
Tom Cruise is being celebrated with a life achievement award from the American Film Institute, AFI's board of trustees said Wednesday. The award will be handed out at a gala tribute in Los Angeles at the Dolby Theatre on April 24 next year.
“Tom Cruise is a global icon,” said Kathleen Kennedy, chair of AFI's board of trustees, in a statement. She praised Cruise's commitment as an actor and producer and his belief in movies' ability to bring people together.
Cruise, 64, has worked in film for more than four decades, starring in movies including “Risky Business,” “A Few Good Men,” “Jerry Maguire,” “Minority Report” and the “Mission: Impossible” series. He has received three Academy Award nominations for acting: best actor in “Born on the Fourth of July” and “Jerry Maguire” and supporting actor for “Magnolia.”
Related video above: Tom Cruise discusses 'Top Gun,' Blue Angels in 1986 interview
As a producer, Cruise was nominated when “Top Gun: Maverick” received a best picture nomination.
Last year, he received an honorary Oscar at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences' Governors Awards.
The AFI Life Achievement Award, established in 1973, recognizes a person whose work has advanced film and stood the test of time. Cruise will join a roster that includes John Ford, Bette Davis, Sidney Poitier, Steven Spielberg, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman and Eddie Murphy, who received the honor earlier this year.
Proceeds from the tribute gala support AFI's education and arts initiatives.

title: BIPARTISAN PERSPECTIVE: Super rich buy the media
text:
I was holding a sign about stopping climate change on a Main Street sidewalk in Waterville this week, and a passing motorist yelled something like, “The media has you by the – collar!” Only he wasn’t quite as polite as that. And I realized he was onto something.
The media lies to us in a way that makes us demonize the other side of any dispute. Media get money by attracting listeners, and anything that inflames anger and blaming makes us want to listen. Lies and exaggerations often do this better than the truth.
But who benefits from this? 1. The media that get paid for doing this; and 2. whoever pays them to lie. Someone wants to sell more oil, or they want to be in power, so they pay the media to say that they are righteous and their opponents are villains: stupid, evil people who want the country to fail. And now they can sell their product, or become a Senator.
Unfortunately, this divides our nation. The truth is that conservatives and liberals both want our country to be great now and in our children’s future. But now, one-third of the country distrusts and hates another third. In the government, they try to defeat everything that the other third tries to do. The resulting gridlock prevents our country’s problems from being solved. And just as bad, we elect representatives who are more and more extreme and radical, unqualified, and rageful.
Forty years ago, the Federal. Communication Commission (FCC) regulated the media concerning truthfulness by enforcing the Fairness Doctrine. Media outlets had to present opposing viewpoints on controversial issues. This made it much harder to get away with lying to us.
Then, in 1987, the FCC repealed the Fairness Doctrine, and the media responded by broadcasting inflammatory positions based merely on opinion, with no opposing information. And so Americans are now misinformed. We get media that lie and distort reality, and Americans find themselves in opposing silos that hate each other.
In 2010, the Supreme Court issued the Citizens United ruling, which allowed unlimited spending on media buys by corporations and other organizations, and the ultra-rich can also buy our elections with unlimited funds, thanks to our Supreme Court rulings. Elon Musk is burying our current elections with $90.5 million so far, and he spent $290 million in the 2024 election cycle.
In summary, corporations and the super-rich buy the media, and the media swamps us with misleading ads that lie and villainize political candidates. This is how Big Money controls our government. Our Senate race in particular has been bought by Big Money from out of State.
Somehow, we have to get Big Money out of government and stop its control of the media. And we have to find a way to enforce truthfulness in the media. It’s time to start demanding this of our politicians.

Maine candidates for governor set to appear at Portland business forum
Maine's three candidates for governor are set to appear Wednesday morning at a Portland Regional Chamber of Commerce forum focused on the issues facing the state and its business community.
Maine candidates for governor set to appear at Portland business forum
Maine's three candidates for governor are set to appear Wednesday morning at a Portland Regional Chamber of Commerce forum focused on the issues facing the state and its business community.
Democrat Hannah Pingree, Republican Bobby Charles and independent Rick Bennett are scheduled to participate in the chamber's Eggs & Issues gubernatorial forum at USM's Hannaford Hall.
The candidates will appear individually and answer the same set of questions, rather than participating in a traditional debate. The forum will be moderated by Portland Regional Chamber President and CEO Quincy Hentzel and Robb Atkinson, board chair of the Portland Community Chamber.
The chamber says topics are expected to include housing, workforce issues, healthcare, taxes, federal policies and the relationship between Greater Portland and Augusta.
The forum is described as an opportunity for business and community leaders to hear directly from the candidates about their priorities ahead of the November election.
The forum comes after the candidates faced off on WMTW's debate stage, where they outlined their positions on a number of issues, including immigration, education, rural healthcare and relief checks.

title: Nearly 100 cases of norovirus reported inside one elementary school, health officials say
text:
OVERLAND PARK, Kan. (KCTV/Gray News) - Health officials have confirmed a norovirus outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Kansas after nearly 100 cases were reported over the past week.
Johnson County Department of Health and Environment Director Charlie Hunt said the total case count has grown to 97, with 95 of those cases inside the school among students and staff, plus two more among family members outside the school.
Hunt said that number is likely an undercount because of how contagious norovirus is.
JCDHE said two cases have been confirmed by lab testing.
Health officials noted the remaining cases are considered epidemiologically linked, meaning people experienced similar symptoms at the same time in the same setting.
Norovirus is highly contagious, causing vomiting and diarrhea. It spreads easily in schools where students and staff are in close contact, health experts said.
Hunt said there are about 2,500 norovirus outbreaks reported each year nationally, and that figure is also likely an undercount.
Hunt said norovirus is sometimes referred to as a ‘stomach flu’ but is not related to influenza. He said norovirus primarily causes vomiting and diarrhea, while influenza is primarily a respiratory illness. Hunt said there is no vaccine for norovirus, and antibiotics are not effective because it is a viral infection.
To prevent transmission, officials urge frequent handwashing with soap and water, thorough cleaning and disinfection of contaminated surfaces, and staying home when sick.
Health officials urged anyone who gets norovirus to stay home for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop.

title: Pope Leo’s doctors confirm he needs no further treatment for lung cancer
text:
VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV will need no further treatment for lung cancer after tests confirmed the disease was localized, the Vatican said Wednesday.
Leo, 71, had part of one lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. Leo was discharged from Rome’s Gemelli Polyclinic on Saturday, four days after surgery, and said he would gradually resume his activities.
The pope’s personal physician, Dr. Luigi Carbone, and his surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora, said the final tests on tissue removed during the surgery confirmed the diagnosis and that the cancer had not spread.
“A subsequent oncology assessment confirmed that no further treatment is necessary,” the doctors said in a statement.
The pope had the lower section, or lobe, of his right lung removed to try to ensure that all the cancer was removed.
Additional treatment is offered for patients whose cancer has spread, such as into the lymph nodes, or who have certain other signs that their cancer might be particularly aggressive. Surgery often can be enough when tumors are caught very early, such as when someone has an X-ray or other scan that shows a spot long before it’s large or causing symptoms.
The pope appears to have had one of those “incidental findings,” a nodule in his lung spotted during another exam.
In an interview with Vatican News on Saturday, Margaritora, the chief thoracic surgeon at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, confirmed that the nodule was found by chance during routine abdominal examinations, and that the pope had not been experiencing any symptoms.
“The statements suggest that this is a stage I lung cancer for which surgery is highly effective and expected to be curative,” said Dr. Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center. He said the lack of further treatment suggests a relatively small cancer, and that it had not spread to lymph nodes.
The pope carried on business while in the hospital, including a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, and has appeared strong in two public appearances at the Vatican since his surgery: the traditional Sunday blessing from a window overlooking St. Peter’s Square and Wednesday’s longer audience in the square, greeting the faithful from around the world.
“Thank you! Thank you for the support of your prayers,” Leo said during the audience.
His next major engagement is an ambitious Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
Margaritora told Vatican News that there was “no clinical reason” to prevent the trip, which includes a dozen flights, two helicopter rides and high altitude stops.
The pope had revealed that a nodule would be surgically removed during the traditional Sunday blessing on Oct. 11, in an unusually transparent disclosure broadcast on live television that broke the tradition of secrecy surrounding papal health issues.
____
AP medical writer Lauran Neergaard contributed to this report.

What ad spending reveals about the state of key Senate races
text:
What ad spending reveals about the state of key Senate races
Experts say where parties spend limited resources can offer clues about where elections are tightening.
What ad spending reveals about the state of key Senate races
Experts say where parties spend limited resources can offer clues about where elections are tightening.
Campaigns are flooding the airwaves in the final two weeks before Election Day, and political ad spending this cycle is already setting records.
The price tag — more than $10 billion in combined aired ad spending and future reservations — has now topped the previous midterm election high set in 2022 and could surpass spending in the 2024 presidential election season, according to data compiled by media-tracking firm AdImpact.
Experts say more ad spending doesn't necessarily translate to more wins, but where parties spend limited resources can offer clues about the direction of key elections.
Republicans are trying to maintain control of both chambers of Congress, but AdImpact found the party is putting far more resources into defending its Senate majority. New data posted Tuesday puts Republican ad spending in the ten most competitive Senate races at $1.03 billion, far exceeding Democrats' $710 million.
Both parties are spending the most in Ohio's Senate race, with a combined $467 million in the general election as of Oct. 20. That's followed by Senate contests in Texas ($368M), Michigan (220M), Maine ($208M), Iowa ($203M), Alaska ($90.5M), New Hampshire ($77.6M), Kansas ($60M), South Carolina ($33.8M), and Minnesota ($7.1M).
"When you get into the fall, you watch where the money goes, and you can see those are the races that are tightening up," said Brendan Glavin, director of insights for Open Secrets, which researches money in politics.
Glavin said the big spending in historically red states like Texas, Iowa, and Kansas is "very unusual." He said it could signal that Republicans are worried about losing in those places.
"They may still feel like they have the edge, but if your opponent is putting in a lot of resources and they're doing well, then you can't sit idle and not be on the air yourself," Glavin said.
In another sign of shifting battlegrounds, Republicans have pulled back spending in states where Democrats have widened their edge in recent months, according to the Cook Political Report.
AdImpact figures found the GOP is slated to spend $3.5 million in Georgia in the final two weeks, compared to $9.5 million from Democrats. In North Carolina, where President Donald Trump is campaigning on Tuesday, Republicans are expected to spend just $2.4 million in the final push, while Democrats are shelling out $14.4 million to try to flip the seat.
The parties also differ in how they're paying for their ads.
AdImpact found Democratic candidates are outspending their Republican counterparts, but Republicans have received much more money from outside groups. That's driving the GOP's overall cash advantage, although candidates are charged a lower advertising rate than Super PACs.
The Trump-aligned Super PAC, MAGA Inc., has been a major source of Republican funding. In a Tuesday social media post, Trump said he plans to spend over $400 million by Election Day.

title: Frequent daytime naps linked to 48% greater risk of dementia, study says
text:
Frequent daytime naps linked to 48% greater risk of dementia, study says
Older adults who nap frequently may face a higher risk of dementia, according to a 10-year study of nearly 1,000 Medicare beneficiaries.
Researchers found that people who napped most days or every day had a 48% higher risk of developing dementia than those who rarely or never napped.
The study, recently published in The Journals of Gerontology, followed 995 adults age 65 and older who showed no signs of cognitive impairment when researchers began tracking them in 2013.
Related video above | Women over 50: Never ignore these Alzheimer's signs
Falling asleep unintentionally during the day was linked to a 39% higher dementia risk, the study found, while naps lasting 30 minutes or less were linked to a 40% higher risk.
The connection between longer naps and dementia was less clear after researchers accounted for nighttime sleep quality.
The link between frequent napping and dementia remained even after researchers considered participants’ health, nighttime sleep and other factors. It also held when researchers excluded people diagnosed with dementia during the first five years of the study. That suggests changes in daytime sleep may appear years before a dementia diagnosis, although the study cannot show why the two are connected, researchers said.
The researchers said frequent napping may also be an early sign of changes in the brain rather than a cause of dementia.
Researchers added the study does not mean that people who nap will develop dementia, and the findings do not establish that napping causes the disease. The team said future studies using wearable sleep monitors and clinical evaluations could help confirm the results.
For now, researchers say changes in daytime sleep could be one clue to watch as scientists work to better understand dementia risk.

title: Employee fatally stabs woman after complaining about work hours, documents say
text:
Employee fatally stabs woman after complaining about work hours, documents say
A Pennsylvania man was taken into custody after officials said he stabbed a fellow employee to death at a local business over a "lack of hours."
Officials said 63-year-old Clifton Emerson Sr., of Harrisburg, was taken into custody in Maryland by Maryland State Police.
Swatara Township police detectives from Pennsylvania are on their way to Maryland as part of the ongoing investigation.
Hearst sister station WGAL obtained court documents that reveal new details about what investigators reported finding and what they think happened at Factory Motor Parts in Swatara Township.
The following information may be disturbing to some viewers.
Video below: Employee killed woman after complaining about hours
Employees find body
Two employees arrived for work shortly before 8 a.m. on Oct. 20, court documents stated.
Once inside, the employees noticed a spilled coffee cup on the hallway floor, a large hole in the drywall next to the cup, and a large pool of blood leading into their boss's office.
One of the employees looked through the window of the office and saw their colleague lying on the ground. Believing she was dead, the two employees left the office and called 911.
When officers arrived, they found the woman's body. She has been identified as Mary Kelly, 57, of West Hanover Township.
Officials said Kelly appeared to have suffered stab wounds to the head and neck.
Evidence found on site
According to court papers, police said they found a trail of bloody footprints that led from the crime scene to an adjacent warehouse.
"The footprints led into the warehouse and next to a large trash can. Inside the can were two blood-covered kitchen-type knives and what appeared to be hair," the affidavit said.
A security employee at the business shared video with police showing Kelly arriving for work and disarming the alarm system. A couple of minutes later, a red SUV pulled in.
Police said she did not appear to notice the SUV.
A couple of minutes later, the man who was in the SUV disappeared from camera view under the roof leading to the front entrance.
Police said no one else entered the building.
The man left about 10 minutes later.
Complaints about work hours
Police said one employee told them another employee, Clifton Emerson Sr., who had worked there for about four years, drove a vehicle like the one seen in the video. That same worker said Emerson had been "complaining about a lack of hours and not having enough money to pay his rent in the past week."
Police said Kelly and Emerson were the only ones in the building until she was discovered dead.
Based on the information and evidence found at the scene, charges were filed against Emerson and a request for an arrest warrant was made.
An autopsy was scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 22.

title: VETERANS CORNER: Delving into the Special Monthly Compensation issue
text:
Recently and issue of greater than normal concern has been the pursuit of that which would be part of a veteran’s disability ratings. It’s called by its acronym (SMC) which means Special Monthly Compensation.
SPECIAL means your need is not in the normal realm. Regular VA income is for those of us who are military injured in one way or another. Special income, is what that injury requires of you in regards to daily need. You have to have someone in your life to help you. Not all vets need that, but some do. You don’t need to be 100 percent disabled to receive this benefit.
Monthly, of course, refers to a period of time. We are paid monthly as regular vets or vets receiving Special Monthly Compensation. This is done by the government in most cases, by direct deposit. I would add the USA doesn’t like sending money outside of the USA but it can be done, perhaps and most likely, with foreign fees. A form 1199-1 must be processed to accomplish this. We have 50,000 x-military in the islands surrounding the Philippines, so for some it’s worth the extra time and fee to do so. It’s referred to as International Direct Transfer. Also, your money gets usually changed to local currency. They like our dollars. USA doesn’t usually charge a conversion fee, depends on the bank. Usually to avoid this, you can go from your bank through another, such as Chase Manhattan to avoid international. Then it’s considered a local exchange. At least that’s the way it use to be.
So, at 30 percent, realistically SMC can begin as the injury will match the percentage, so to speak. An example I would give is say, loss of use of a limb, such as a foot or a hand. Those are usually in 30 percent areas. So, if you receive what we refer to as a 2507 exam, commonly referred to now as a Comp & Pen Exam, and they decide (VA) that your limb is damaged enough to be considered effective loss of use, then they will assign you a SMC evaluation called or referred to as “K” level. It becomes permanent disability that you will keep forever unless you recover, or you have committed fraud. “K” is forever other than what I have stated, and is on the bottom of the SMC list of ratings.
OK, now we have explained what SMC is, now we can address the more intrical part of this area. In past chapters I have discussed the different levels of cause. They all have, their advantages, and that is mostly money. None are easily obtained unless you are in different degrees of disability. Most of the time the veteran is already at 100 percent disability. We can go over that again in later issues as there are always new veterans, with minor and serious degrees of injury, as well as different types. Multiple 100 percent totals are very possible depending on the injury, time, pain and loss. There are also emotional types of injuries. Those are currently being revisited. A basic current list of SMC conditions, as I said begins with “K”. Then we have S – housebound, L – needs help daily and A&A. Then we have L-1/2, M, M1/2, N, N1/2, O, R-1, and certainly not least R-2= more professional help and receives more money. This becomes extreme home care. “K” as I stated is at the bottom but one of my favorites as it can be added on top of L or R-1 – so vet can have, say, “L” + K -, two SMC’s. That means L income plus K pay together not just one. I believe you can still receive three K awards.
So now it’s time to answer the R-1 debate. If you can stand you don’t qualify for R-1. Ability regarding standing is contrary to law. (38 USC 1114(r)(i) 38CFR 3.350(h) does not require inability to stand, it requires O/P plus need for A&A, plus need for daily personal healthcare services 38CFR 3.352(b), case in point, Kemp vs. Shulkin, limited standing does not establish effective function. Read the law. It’s in your computer or law library. The State of Maine has a wonderfully staffed Law Library.
This is my conclusion on a very complex group of issues which in my opinion shouldn’t be. I am a firm believer that the level of care and it’s acquisition should be available and understandable to the lay person. Anyone can review the law and the cases that have been tried, won and lost.
That being said – law beats rumor or backroom lawyers or pseudo-intellectuals. Although some have very good intensions they are misleading and absolutely wrong in giving misleading direction. I will give you one example of a 85-year-old man who visited VA 60 years ago seeking help and was told he didn’t qualify because he made too much money. I believe the person speaking with this veteran was new, poorly trained, and lacked of needed knowledge and compassion required of someone giving that sort of conclusion.
I was supposed to be retiring from doing this but the compassion of my wife rubbed off on me, so, I listened to his story from our own VA emergency room. He was only there to bring his disabled son and being a true to life Down Easter, started talking to my wife, who was delivering this very paper to the emergency department. He broke my wife’s heart with his story and history. When I joined my wife she coerced me into speaking with this gentleman. I was totally shocked and heartbroken after hearing what he shared. In the end I told him, I couldn’t do anything that evening but if he wanted to come to my house on the following day, I would be free.
He drove from down east to Togus with what little he could find for records. He had a DD-214. I took him to VA after spending a couple of hours writing his history and looking at medical records he had saved and paid for through the years. On that one day I had him signed into the VA system, had a doctor assigned, and wrote a 12 issue case and filed it. My wife and I left for Asia to help veterans in the islands. When we returned he came to our home teary eyed and thanked God and us. In that short period of time, less than a year, he became a 100 percent P&T veteran. This is a verifiable true story of a great man, veteran, who was injured in service who went 60 years on his own dime until he fortuitously met my extremely sensitive and compassionate wife in the very place that he once was denied by a poorly trained adviser. He lost 60 years of medical and financial aid; Who’s to blame?
In conclusion let me give you some advise that is verifiable.
Conclusion- Law beats rumor,
Standing “does not” defeat R-1- The law is clear.
R-1 has no standing test 38USC 1114(r)(i) – requires (i) entitlement to O designation. If VSO tells you there is a standing test, he doesn’t read the law. He is applying a test that Congress never wrote, VA never regulated, and CAVC rejected in Kemp. Showing “medical “need daily under 3.352(b), Bowel Bladder, Skin, feeding – show O/P predicate, with your 100 percent + ratings – I will try to give you some cases for you to review that are understandable. Tell us if you don’t and I/we will clarify all. There is so much and I am allowed only so much space to write for you.
1. Kemp vs.Shulkin, 28 vet.app. 386 (2016)= lost use test- standing briefly “does not” kill R-1 claim (Fake leg test)
2. Breniser vs. Shinseki, 2011- K money adds on top of R-1 or “L”. you can have 2 SMC’s
3. Turco vs. Brown, 1993 – VA must look at “real need” for help, not one trick like standing.
4. Balaza vs. McDonald – Many 100% can make SMC”O” level.

title: Maine judge greenlights state’s initial approval of Juniper Ridge Landfill expansion
text:
A Penobscot County Superior Court justice has backed the state’s finding that expanding Juniper Ridge Landfill is in the public interest, according to a release from the challengers, clearing the way for the project to move forward.
“This ruling is a setback, but it can’t bury the truth that the Penobscot Nation and local residents have brought into the open — that this landfill is part of a broken system that puts polluters’ wallets over people’s health,” Alex St. Pierre, vice president for environmental justice at Conservation Law Foundation, said in a statement. “The knowledge, persistence and power of these communities have already shifted the conversation — and that momentum will carry forward until justice is served.”
The Maine Department of Environmental Protection first issued a positive public benefit determination for the expansion in October 2024, but the Penobscot Nation and Conservation Law Foundation appealed the decision.
In January, Justice Bruce Mallonee struck down that determination, and in March the department again found that the expansion was in the public interest. The groups returned to court in July, where opponents argued the state has continued to fail to meet environmental justice standards.
But in a statement Tuesday, the Penobscot Nation and Conservation Law Foundation said Mallonee ruled in favor of the department.
“We have fought pollution, injustice and decades of harm to heal the Penobscot River, a relative that has sustained our people since time immemorial and continues to sustain communities across Maine,” Penobscot Nation Tribal Chief Kirk Francis said. “We are not asking the state to undo generations of harm overnight. We are asking it not to take us backward. Our cultural survival is tied to the health of the Penobscot River, and there is too much at stake to keep adding to the harms it already carries.”
More than half of Maine’s landfill waste ends up at Juniper Ridge. It is owned by the state through the Bureau of General Services, which has an operating contract with NEWSME Landfill Operations, a subsidiary of waste management company Casella.
The landfill is expected to reach capacity in 2028, and in order for Casella to apply for a license to expand, the Department of Environmental Protection must determine the expansion would benefit the public.

title: Eighth-Grader's Double-OT Winner Highlights Madawaska Soccer Sweep
text:
The County Scoreboard: Eighth-Grader Delivers Double-OT Winner as Madawaska Sweeps Washburn
An eighth-grader provided the biggest moment of Tuesday's County soccer action, helping Madawaska pull out a double-overtime victory over Washburn as the regular season reaches its final day.
Dani Pelletier scored just 57 seconds into the second overtime to give the Lady Owls a 1-0 victory over the Beavers.
Madawaska's boys also picked up a win, defeating Washburn 6-1 behind a pair of goals from Josh Querze.
The two victories came with the regular season winding down and teams preparing for the start of tournament soccer later this week.
Girls Soccer: Pelletier's Double-OT Goal Lifts Madawaska Past Washburn
Madawaska and Washburn needed more than regulation and one overtime period to settle Tuesday's girls soccer matchup.
The two teams remained scoreless through regulation and the first overtime before eighth-grader Dani Pelletier delivered the game-winner just 57 seconds into the second overtime.
The goal gave Madawaska a 1-0 victory in one of the closest games of the final week of the regular season.
For Pelletier, it was a big moment at an important point in the season, providing the Lady Owls with a victory just before the postseason begins.
Boys Soccer: Querze Scores Twice in Madawaska Victory
Madawaska's boys completed the sweep of Washburn with a 6-1 victory.
Josh Querze led the Owls with two goals, while Aiden Gagnon, Oliver Pelkey, Bradley Kennedy and Ashton Guerrette each added one.
Owen Rackliffe scored Washburn's lone goal.
The Owls spread their scoring among five players in another strong offensive showing as the regular season draws to a close.
Soccer Playoffs Are Almost Here
Wednesday, October 21, marks the final countable day of the regular season, and the focus is quickly shifting toward tournament soccer.
For teams across Aroostook County, the next few days will bring the final standings, playoff seedings and tournament matchups.
The first regional preliminary games in eight-player soccer are scheduled for Friday, October 23, with preliminary games in the other classifications following Saturday, October 24.
Regional quarterfinals are scheduled for October 27 and 28.
There are plenty of County teams with reasons to be excited about the postseason.
Presque Isle's girls are looking toward a high seed in Class B North after an impressive regular season, while teams such as Caribou, Fort Kent, Houlton, Central Aroostook, Katahdin, Wisdom, Van Buren, Madawaska and several other County programs will be watching closely as their tournament positions are finalized.
Some teams will have an opportunity to host playoff games, while others will be preparing for road trips with their seasons on the line.
We'll have a closer look at the final standings, County tournament matchups and the games worth watching once the brackets are set.

title: China transfer station supervisor intends to retire in 2027
text:
At the Oct. 13 meeting of China’s Transfer Station Committee, Committee Chairman Benjamin Weymouth said he hopes a successor will be chosen in 2026, so Maraggio can train the new person and retire on schedule. Town Manager Rebecca Hapgood said there were already two applications for the position.
Maraggio said after the meeting he’s worked at the transfer station since May 2022, and became supervisor in June 2022.
The other two major topics at the Oct. 13 meeting were local solid waste haulers and disposal at the Municipal WasteHub, in Hampden.
A resident was concerned about the apparent rumor that the China facility will be closed to local haulers. She hires someone to pick up her trash, she said, and appreciates the convenience and the fact that she is helping support a small local business.
Hapgood said there is no plan to ban commercial haulers. The select board might discuss a 2027 rate increase for them, perhaps at the Nov. 2 board meeting.
The issue that sometimes arises, she said, is that a hauler’s route includes more than one town, so the truck brings in out-of-town waste that is not supposed to be accepted.
When Weymouth explained that low fees meant taxpayers were subsidizing the haulers, the resident replied that families without children subsidize China schools. And, she told Hapgood and committee members, individuals also bring in out-of-town waste, usually to oblige a family member or friend.
Hapgood said the Municipal WasteHub is operating, though there are still on-going improvements, including new robot arms shown on the organization’s Facebook page. There are more than 40 employees, and the operation is expanding to two shifts daily.
Committee members would like to visit the facility, as they have done once before.
In other business, Maraggio reported the transfer station’s composting services are being well used.
He has been collecting price quotes for a replacement compactor, a project proposed for next spring. Prices are “all over the place,” he said. Hapgood said the replacement reserve fund has $50,000 available.
Maraggio proposed considering shortening hours during the winter, so the transfer station would not be open so long after dark. His main concern is safety.
Weymouth commented that the draft Solid Waste Ordinance, which voters will accept or reject at the polls on Nov. 3, “looked good to me.”
Committee members scheduled their next meeting for Tuesday, Nov. 17 (third instead of usual second Tuesday), at 8:30 a.m. in the town office meeting room (instead of the usual 9 a.m., to avoid conflict with the group that uses the room at 10 a.m.).

title: MAINE-LY GARDENING: An ancient tree for your yard?
text:
The Ginkgo is a tree we most often associate with Asia but will grow well in Central Maine and many other places around the world. You may have seen them in the median strip of Western Avenue, in Augusta, as they are frequently chosen as street trees due to their ability to tolerate pollution from traffic as well as other strengths.
The ginkgoes we see are the last descendants of an ancient family of plants that were the first to develop true seeds. Earlier plants were more like our modern ferns. The ginkgo of today is almost unchanged from those that lived along with the dinosaurs of the Jurassic period. If you travel to Washington State, you can visit a large petrified ginkgo forest. Ginkgoes survived the last Ice Age in China and were among the first trees cultivated by humans. In Japan there are ginkgoes that were planted around monasteries 1,000 years ago and some may be much older. In addition to resistance to pollution, the ginkgo’s long life as attributed to resistance to disease and insects.
Fall has been considered the best time for tree planting in New England, but our drought conditions have made us reconsider this. However, horticulturists have found that ginkgoes are best planted after the last spring frost. This allows them to establish their roots in the warmer months. They are hardy, long-lived trees but appreciate this gentle start. If you believe you’ll be able to provide enough water next summer, consider a ginkgo for an attractive shade tree that will live for centuries.
In spring the bright green fan-shaped leaves with two lobes emerge. That shape gives the species name bilabial. The autumn leaves become bright yellow. Some ginkgoes are famous form dropping all of their leaves in one day. I know of one on a university campus in Michigan and another in Hartford, Connecticut, which have become the focus of local betting on the leaf drop – like our ice-out contests.
Check local nurseries for the varieties of ginkgoes on offer. In addition to the typical trees that will grow somewhat slowly during its first two decades, it will mature to 50 feet high or taller, branching out to 20 feet in all directions, there are a number of miniature ginkgoes on the market which can fit a small space in the yard or make a nice addition to a rock garden.
Because the fruit-like structures that contain the seeds on female plants can smell like rancid butter, male trees are the most commonly planted. In New York City there is a neighborhood that was planted with female gingkoes years ago and residents avoid stepping on the fallen seeds in autumn. The potentially smelly seeds of female ginkgo trees have traditional medicinal uses, but scientists caution us to be careful of the various preparations as some of the chemicals are produced by the plant are poisonous. The seeds can also be used in cooking in certain manners. In general, only male plants are sold in nurseries, but check to be sure of the sex of the trees you’ll see.
Ginkgoes have a much longer and more complicated story to explore if you enjoy studying natural history. And, if you happen to know of a local ginkgo, like the one in front of Erskine Academy, on Rte. 32, in South China, see if its leaves drop on just one day.
 © Judith Chute Hsiang
Jude Hsiang is a retired Extension Master Gardener Program instructor and a member of the China Community Garden.

title: Woman accused of intentionally crashing into oncoming semi, killing 73-year-old passenger
text:
PIKE COUNTY, Ill. (WGEM/Gray News) — An Illinois woman has been arrested on first-degree murder charges following a July crash that investigators allege was intentional.
Pike County Sheriff David Greenwood said deputies responded July 24 at 7:54 p.m. to a head-on collision between a passenger car and a semitruck pulling a trailer on U.S. 54 near the top of Atlas Hill.
Three occupants in the passenger vehicle were injured and taken to a hospital, Greenwood said.
One of those passengers, 73-year-old Cherie Wells of Pittsfield, later died from her injuries in St. Louis County, Missouri.
Deputies determined during the investigation that the driver, identified as Jaime Rhode of Griggsville, purposely steered in front of the oncoming semi with the intent to kill all occupants in her vehicle, Greenwood said.
An arrest warrant was signed Friday charging Rhode with two counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder.
Rhode was arrested Tuesday and booked in the Pike County Jail.
